styleDirection.name: Friendly workshop
styleDirection.summary: Warm and hands-on, like a neighborhood repair bench: approachable enough for someone who has never asked for help, calm enough to feel like a small good deed rather than a chore.

primary.name: Workshop Teal
primary.usage: Primary buttons (Snap a photo, Book a spot), active tab, progress indicator.

secondary.name: Copper Tool
secondary.usage: Accent for the next-event date chip, item-type highlights, and empty-state illustrations. Use sparingly so it stays a highlight.

semantic.name: Almost Full
semantic.usage: Event nearly full, photo too dark to read.

semantic.name: Needs Attention
semantic.usage: Missing description, upload failed, field errors.

semantic.name: Bring List Blue
semantic.usage: "What to bring" hints and repair-cafe rules.

surfacesAndText.name: Card White
surfacesAndText.usage: Cards, list rows, bottom sheets, form fields.

typefaces.rationale: Rounded geometry feels friendly without looking childish, and it stays legible when the phone is held at a distance during a photo.
Neutral, highly readable on small screens for addresses, dates and form text.

scale.usage: Distance, event date chips, helper text.

lineHeightAndSpacing.letterSpacing: 0 for body, -0.01em for Display and Title
lineHeightAndSpacing.paragraphSpacing: 12px between paragraphs, 8px between a title and its subtext
notes: Keep a 16px minimum for anything the user has to read or type.
Limit list-row copy to two lines and truncate the rest so rows stay a predictable height.

layoutGrid.notes: Single-column flow. Cards span all 4 columns; the item-type chips on onboarding use a 2-up layout of 2 columns each.

spacingSystem.usage: Use 16px inside cards, 24px between cards, and 32px between major sections.

whiteSpace: Leave at least 24px above the primary button so it never crowds the last field.
Put the primary action in the bottom third of the screen for one-handed reach, with 16px clear space beneath it plus the safe area.
One idea per screen: onboarding, photo, list and confirmation each get their own space rather than sharing one.

levels.name: Base
levels.usage: Screen background and flat text areas.

levels.name: Card
levels.usage: Repair cafe cards and list rows.

levels.name: Sticky bar
levels.usage: Bottom action bar holding the primary button.

levels.name: Sheet
levels.usage: Photo source picker and booking bottom sheets, over a 40% scrim.

dropShadow.color: rgba(30, 43, 39, 0.10) to 0.20 (tinted from Bench Ink, never pure black)
dropShadow.notes: Shadows point upward for bottom-anchored elements so they read as lifting off the screen edge.

visualPriority: The primary button is the only element with a filled Teal background on each screen.
Cards stay quiet at level 1 so the sheet at level 3 clearly owns attention when it opens.
Use the Copper accent for one highlight per card at most, such as the next event date.

styleDirection.name: Quiet utility
styleDirection.summary: A compact, native-feeling popup that disappears into the browser. Dense but calm, so a researcher with 30 tabs can scan and save in one glance.

primary.name: Stash Indigo
primary.usage: Save group and Restore all buttons, focus rings, checked checkboxes.

secondary.name: Marker Amber
secondary.usage: Tab count badges and the most recently saved group indicator.

semantic.name: Duplicate Amber
semantic.usage: Duplicate group name, tabs that cannot be restored.

semantic.name: Hint Blue
semantic.usage: Inline tips such as "Pinned tabs are skipped".

surfacesAndText.name: Row White
surfacesAndText.usage: Tab rows, group rows, input fields.

typefaces.fallback: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
typefaces.rationale: The brief requires system fonts only, so hierarchy comes from weight and size instead of a second typeface.

typefaces.fallback: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
typefaces.rationale: Matches the browser chrome so the popup feels native and loads instantly.

scale.usage: Popup header and group names on the detail view.
Hostnames and tab counts. Never go below 12px.

notes: Truncate tab titles to one line with an ellipsis and show the full title in a tooltip.
Use tabular numerals for tab counts so badges align down the list.

layoutGrid.notes: Header (48px) and footer action bar (56px) are fixed, and the middle list scrolls. That keeps Save and Restore always visible without scrolling.

spacingSystem.usage: Rows are 40px tall with 12px horizontal padding, and controls use 8px gaps.

whiteSpace: Density is a feature here, but keep at least 8px between rows and their checkboxes so targets do not blur together.
Do not add empty-state illustrations; a single line of text and one button is enough within 600px height.
Keep 12px of padding around the popup edge, since the browser adds its own frame.

levels.name: Flat
levels.usage: Popup background and rows, separated by 1px dividers.

levels.name: Sticky bar
levels.usage: Footer with Save group and Restore all.

levels.name: Menu
levels.usage: Overflow menu and tooltips.

dropShadow.notes: The browser already draws a shadow around the whole popup, so inner layers stay minimal to avoid a double-shadow look.

visualPriority: Rely on dividers and fills over shadows, and reserve elevation for the footer and menus.
The footer button is the only solid Indigo fill, so the next action is obvious.
Selected rows get a light indigo tint and a 3px left bar instead of a shadow.

styleDirection.name: Calm focus
styleDirection.summary: A quiet daily planner that feels like a clear desk. Restrained color, strong hierarchy, and one obvious top priority so the day never feels overwhelming.

primary.name: Focus Slate Blue
primary.usage: Add task button, selected task row, focus rings.

secondary.name: Priority Coral
secondary.usage: Marks the #1 priority task and the streak counter in the summary. One coral element on screen at a time.

semantic.name: Done Green
semantic.usage: Completed tasks and the end-of-day summary check.

typefaces.rationale: Sturdy and slightly technical, which suits a productivity tool without feeling cold.
One family keeps a small window uncluttered. Pair with IBM Plex Mono for task times.

scale.usage: Task titles in the ranked list.
Times and rank numbers, set in tabular figures.

notes: Rank numbers use tabular figures so 1 through 9 align in a column.
Keep task titles to one line at 16px and let long titles truncate; full text appears in the edit modal.

layoutGrid.columns: 12 columns inside a fixed 600 x 400 window
layoutGrid.notes: Header takes 56px and the list scrolls in the remaining ~344px. Tasks span all 12 columns; the modal spans columns 2 to 11.

spacingSystem.usage: Task rows are 44px with 12px vertical padding, and 24px window margin.

whiteSpace: Show at most 5 tasks before the list scrolls so the window never feels crowded.
Leave 16px clear space around the add button since the window cannot resize.
Give the empty state a generous, centered layout with a single call to action.

levels.name: Window
levels.usage: Window background; the OS draws the window shadow.

levels.name: Task row
levels.usage: Task rows, with a slight lift on hover.

levels.name: Dragging
levels.usage: A task row being reordered.

levels.name: Modal
levels.usage: Add/edit task modal over a 35% scrim.

dropShadow.style: Soft and vertical, offset y only
dropShadow.notes: Never use horizontal offsets; the small window has no room for shadows to spill to the sides.

visualPriority: The top-ranked task gets the coral rank marker and a heavier weight; the rest stay neutral.
The modal is the only level-3 element, so it clearly takes over focus.
Completed tasks fade to secondary text with a green check and drop to level 0.

styleDirection.name: Fresh boutique
styleDirection.summary: Soft, editorial and personal, like a small flower shop window. Lets bouquet photography lead, with quiet color and elegant type that still gets a busy customer to checkout quickly.

primary.name: Deep Rose
primary.usage: Add to cart, Place order, and links.

secondary.name: Leaf Green
secondary.usage: Size selectors, "Ready for pickup" badges, and section accents.

semantic.name: Low Stock Amber
semantic.usage: "Only 2 left today" and unavailable pickup slots.

typefaces.rationale: Elegant high-contrast serif that feels handcrafted and gives the shop a boutique identity.
Clear, friendly sans for prices, forms and buttons, and it stays readable on a phone during a work break.

scale.usage: Section titles and bouquet names on detail page.

lineHeightAndSpacing.letterSpacing: 0 for body; +0.06em for small uppercase labels
notes: Keep body lines to 60 to 70 characters wide on desktop.
Set prices in bold sans, not the serif, so they scan quickly between photos.

layoutGrid.notes: Bouquet cards show 1 per row on mobile, 2 on tablet and 3 or 4 on desktop. Breakpoints at 640px and 1024px.

spacingSystem.usage: Use 24px inside cards, 48px between page sections on mobile, and 96px on desktop.

whiteSpace: Let photos breathe with 24 to 32px around each card; crowding hides the product.
Give the home hero at least 96px of vertical padding on desktop so it feels like a shop window.
Keep the checkout flow narrow (max 640px) with generous spacing to reduce hesitation.

levels.name: Page
levels.usage: Backgrounds and text sections.

levels.name: Card
levels.usage: Bouquet cards.

levels.name: Hover / sticky
levels.usage: Card on hover and the sticky header once the page scrolls.

levels.name: Cart drawer
levels.usage: Cart drawer and pickup time picker over a scrim.

dropShadow.color: Rose-tinted rgba(163, 50, 79, 0.08 to 0.14) for cards; neutral ink for overlays
dropShadow.style: Soft, wide blur with low opacity
dropShadow.notes: Tinting shadows with the brand rose keeps the page warm rather than grey.

visualPriority: Photography is the hero: keep overlays and shadows quiet around images.
Add to cart and Place order are the only solid Deep Rose fills.
The cart drawer at level 3 sits above everything else so checkout feels focused.

styleDirection.name: Big, calm, high-contrast
styleDirection.summary: Gentle but unmistakable. A dark, OLED-friendly interface with very large type and only one action per screen so an older adult can respond confidently with a single tap.

primary.name: Calm Blue
primary.usage: Next-dose time, complication ring and the main Confirm control outline.

secondary.name: Snooze Amber
secondary.usage: Snooze button and a dose that is due soon.

semantic.name: Taken Green
semantic.usage: Confirm taken state and history checkmarks.

semantic.name: Neutral Cyan
semantic.usage: Informational text such as the next reminder.

surfacesAndText.name: OLED Black
surfacesAndText.usage: Screen background; true black saves battery and maximizes contrast.

surfacesAndText.name: Ring Grey
surfacesAndText.usage: Outlines for buttons and history rows.

typefaces.rationale: Designed for low-vision readability; distinct letterforms reduce misreading of dose names and numbers.
A single family keeps the tiny screen simple. Use the platform system font if custom fonts are not available on watch.

scale.usage: Dose time on the reminder and the complication.

notes: Use sentence case and two lines maximum per element.
Use bold weights over thin ones because thin strokes shimmer on small OLED screens.

layoutGrid.margin: 12% inset on round faces / 10pt on square faces
layoutGrid.notes: Stack elements vertically and keep content inside the safe circle. Place the main action in the lower half where the thumb rests.

spacingSystem.usage: Buttons are at least 48pt tall with 8pt between them, so a fumbled tap never hits the wrong one.

whiteSpace: One primary message and one or two buttons per screen; leave the rest black.
Keep at least 8pt between the two buttons to prevent mis-taps.
Avoid content in the corners of round faces where it gets clipped.

levels.name: Base
levels.usage: True black screen background.

levels.name: Raised fill
levels.usage: Charcoal fill #1C1C1F for rows and buttons.

levels.name: Active
levels.usage: Pressed or focused control: lighter fill and 2px colored outline.

dropShadow.notes: Shadows disappear against black and add noise on small OLED screens. Use lighter fills and outlines to show depth instead.

visualPriority: The main action gets the largest tap area, color fill and boldest label.
Snooze is outlined only, so it is available but clearly secondary.
Layering is expressed through lighter surface tones and outlines, never shadows.

styleDirection.name: Bright toybox
styleDirection.summary: Playful, chunky and forgiving. Big rounded shapes, bold color and icon-only controls that a 4 to 7 year old can understand without reading.

primary.name: Sky Blue
primary.usage: Save and Share buttons, selected tool ring.

secondary.name: Sunshine Yellow
secondary.usage: Highlights, celebration moments after saving, and the selected-color halo.

semantic.name: Saved Green
semantic.usage: Drawing saved and sent to the parent device.

semantic.name: Oops Orange
semantic.usage: Gentle prompts, such as "Ask a grown-up".

semantic.name: Friendly Red
semantic.usage: Delete confirmation; always paired with an icon and a parent gate.

surfacesAndText.name: Night Indigo
surfacesAndText.usage: The few text labels, such as parent setup.

surfacesAndText.name: Crayon Line
surfacesAndText.usage: Outlines around tools and gallery tiles.

typefaces.rationale: Round and bubbly with friendly proportions that children respond to.
Rounded terminals and open forms for the small amount of parent-facing text.

scale.usage: The occasional text label under an icon.

notes: Use as little text as possible; every child-facing action needs an icon that works alone.
Set text for adults in higher contrast and at larger sizes than usual for a tablet.

layoutGrid.maxWidth: Full-bleed canvas; chrome inside 1024 x 768 logical points
layoutGrid.notes: Palette dock runs down the left (96px), the canvas takes the centre, and brush sizes sit in a right rail. The layout mirrors for left-handed use.

spacingSystem.usage: Touch targets are at least 72px square with 16px minimum between them.

whiteSpace: Give color swatches 16px between them so small fingers do not hit two at once.
Keep the canvas as large as possible; controls stay in the margins.
Use big empty margins around Save so it cannot be tapped by accident during drawing.

levels.name: Canvas
levels.usage: Flat drawing surface.

levels.name: Sticker
levels.usage: Color swatches and tool buttons: chunky shadow like a physical sticker.

levels.name: Pressed
levels.usage: Button pressed: the shadow shrinks so it sinks into the page.

levels.name: Popup
levels.usage: Save and share dialog over a soft scrim.

dropShadow.style: Hard-edged offset shadow with zero blur for level 1 to 3, giving a toy-like feel
dropShadow.notes: A visible press state (the shadow shrinking) doubles as feedback for children who need to see that a tap registered.

visualPriority: The selected color and tool get a thick yellow halo so state is obvious without reading.
The canvas stays the largest and flattest element; all controls sit around it.
Only one dialog at a time, always centered, with a big Sky Blue action.

styleDirection.name: Kitchen-counter clarity
styleDirection.summary: Warm and appetizing, and readable from across the room with floury hands. Visuals only support the voice: clear listening states and big, glanceable recipe text.

primary.name: Basil Green
primary.usage: Listening ring, primary buttons and active voice-state indicator.

secondary.name: Tomato
secondary.usage: Highlights key ingredients in the recipe and marks the "Try another" action.

semantic.name: Missed Red
semantic.usage: "Sorry, I didn't catch that" state and connection loss.

semantic.name: Prompt Blue
semantic.usage: Suggested phrases the user can say.

typefaces.rationale: A soft, characterful serif that feels like a cookbook and stays readable at large sizes.
Designed to improve reading speed, so steps are easy to read from a distance.

scale.usage: Recipe name on the companion screen.
Current recipe step, readable from arm's length or more.
Time, servings and the "You can say" hints.

lineHeightAndSpacing.letterSpacing: 0 for body; +0.02em on Lexend at small sizes
notes: Voice prompts: keep them to 12 words or fewer, with the question at the end.
Every confirmation repeats the key words, such as "Chicken, rice, and onions. Is that right?"

layoutGrid.columns: 4 columns (companion screen); voice flow uses a turn-taking sequence rather than a grid
layoutGrid.notes: Companion content is a single large column so it can be read without touching. Ingredients and steps stack; no side-by-side panels.

spacingSystem.usage: Use 24px between ingredient lines and 40px between recipe sections for easy scanning.

whiteSpace: One step at a time: show the current step large and hide the rest behind a small "Next" hint.
Leave 48px of space around the listening indicator so its state is unmistakable.
Do not fill the screen; empty space helps the cook find their place when glancing back.

levels.name: Base
levels.usage: Screen background.

levels.name: Card
levels.usage: Recipe and ingredient cards.

levels.name: Listening glow
levels.usage: Pulsing ring around the listening indicator, animated softly.

levels.name: Overlay
levels.usage: Error or "Try again" overlay.

dropShadow.notes: The glow used for listening is a ring, not a shadow, so it reads as a state and not a decoration.

visualPriority: Listening, thinking and speaking each have a distinct color and animation so the state is clear.
The current recipe step is the largest thing on the screen; ingredients sit at a lower level.
Errors use level 3 overlays so they cannot be missed from across the kitchen.

styleDirection.name: Clear and dependable
styleDirection.summary: A straightforward, no-nonsense scheduling tool. Status is communicated through clear color coding and labels so a busy employee on a shared break-room computer can post or claim a shift in under a minute.

primary.name: Shift Navy
primary.usage: Post a shift, Claim shift, and primary navigation.

secondary.name: Open Teal
secondary.usage: Marks open shifts on the board and "Available" tags.

semantic.name: Pending Amber
semantic.usage: Awaiting manager approval and shifts starting soon.

semantic.name: Notice Blue
semantic.usage: Policy notes and "Sign out when finished" reminder.

surfacesAndText.name: Panel White
surfacesAndText.usage: Schedule table, forms and shift cards.

typefaces.rationale: Clean, highly legible and compact, which keeps schedule tables tidy.
Works well on older shared computers with unpredictable displays. Use tabular figures for times and dates.

scale.usage: Shift times and names in dense tables.
Metadata such as who posted the shift.

notes: Use tabular numerals so times line up in columns.
Write dates with weekday first ("Thu, 12 Jun") to match how staff think about shifts.

layoutGrid.maxWidth: 1200px, collapsing to a single column under 768px
layoutGrid.notes: Schedule takes 8 columns and the open shifts board 4 on desktop; they stack on smaller screens. Breakpoints at 768px and 1024px.

spacingSystem.usage: Table rows have 12px vertical padding; forms use 24px between fields.

whiteSpace: Keep table rows at least 48px tall so clicking is easy with a trackpad or an old mouse.
Leave 32px between the schedule and the open shifts board so they read as separate tasks.
Keep forms in a single column, with generous space around the submit button.

levels.name: Page
levels.usage: Backgrounds and table rows.

levels.name: Card
levels.usage: Shift cards on the open board and form panels.

levels.name: Dropdown
levels.usage: Menus and date pickers.

levels.name: Modal
levels.usage: Swap confirmation dialog and session timeout warning.

dropShadow.notes: Pair every card shadow with a 1px border so cards stay visible on low-contrast, older monitors.

visualPriority: Open shifts use Teal tags so they stand out from the user's own shifts.
Status tags (Open, Pending, Swapped) always combine color with a text label, never color alone.
The confirmation modal is the highest level so the final swap step cannot be missed.

styleDirection.name: Neighborly and trustworthy
styleDirection.summary: Generous and warm, but with visible trust signals. Verification, ratings and status are clear and consistent so neighbors feel safe meeting up to share food.

primary.name: Harvest Green
primary.usage: Claim, Post item and Confirm pickup.

secondary.name: Carrot Orange
secondary.usage: Expiry countdowns and "Ending soon" highlights on listings.

semantic.name: Expiring
semantic.usage: Listing about to expire, pickup window closing.

semantic.name: No-show / Expired
semantic.usage: Expired listings, no-shows and failed posts.

surfacesAndText.name: Basket White
surfacesAndText.usage: Listing cards, chat bubbles, bottom sheets.

typefaces.rationale: Slightly rounded and confident, friendly for a community app without feeling childish.
Very readable at small sizes for chat, dates and dietary tags.

scale.usage: Dietary tags and badges, set in uppercase with +0.04em spacing.

notes: Chat bubbles use 15 to 16px body text at 1.4 line height with 8px vertical spacing between messages from the same sender.
Express expiry in words ("Expires in 3 hrs") rather than only a timestamp.

layoutGrid.notes: Listings use a full-width card on list view and a 2-column grid on the map bottom sheet. Chat bubbles are limited to 75% of the width.

spacingSystem.usage: 16px inside cards, 12px between listing cards, and 24px between major groups.

whiteSpace: Leave room around the verified badge so it is noticed but not crammed against names.
Keep the map visible above the bottom sheet; do not cover more than 55% of it at half state.
Separate poster and neighbor flows visually with distinct tab bars and empty states.

levels.name: Base
levels.usage: Screen backgrounds.

levels.name: Listing card
levels.usage: Listing cards and chat bubbles.

levels.name: Map overlay
levels.usage: Map filter chips, floating buttons and selected pin card.

levels.name: Bottom sheet
levels.usage: Listing detail, filters and claim confirmation sheets.

dropShadow.style: Soft with slight upward direction for bottom-anchored elements
dropShadow.notes: Map overlays need stronger shadows than list cards because they float over busy map imagery.

visualPriority: Trust signals (verified badge, rating) use the blue accent and are consistent everywhere.
Expiry uses Carrot and Warning colors only for urgent states so they keep their meaning.
The claim button is the sole solid green fill on the listing detail sheet.

styleDirection.name: Confident data overlay
styleDirection.summary: A crisp, self-contained widget that looks the same on any store. Strong borders and predictable type keep it separate from host pages, and price drops are the one thing that feels celebratory.

primary.name: Watch Indigo
primary.usage: Track this price, Save alert, and the price line on the chart.

secondary.name: Drop Green
secondary.usage: Price-drop indicator, below-target markers on the chart and Go to product.

semantic.name: Target Hit
semantic.usage: Price is at or below the target.

surfacesAndText.name: Overlay White
surfacesAndText.usage: Overlay panel, dashboard cards and chart area.

surfacesAndText.name: Axis Grey
surfacesAndText.usage: Chart axes, store names and dates.

surfacesAndText.name: Overlay Border
surfacesAndText.usage: 1px border that separates the overlay from any host page.

typefaces.rationale: Declare the font explicitly on the overlay so it never inherits a host page's type styles.
Use tabular figures for prices so the numbers align and digits do not jitter as values change.

notes: Reset inherited styles inside the overlay (for example with a shadow root or an all: initial wrapper) so host CSS cannot change size or color.
Always show currency symbols and two decimals, with the change in absolute and percent form ("-$12.00, -8%").

layoutGrid.columns: Overlay: 4 columns in a 340px panel; Popup: single column at 380px wide
layoutGrid.margin: 16px inside panels; 16px inset from the viewport corner
layoutGrid.maxWidth: Overlay 340px wide, docked bottom-right; popup 380 x 560px
layoutGrid.notes: The chart takes the full panel width at 16:9 with a 4 x 4 gridline structure. Dashboard rows show thumbnail, name, current price and target price on one line.

spacingSystem.usage: 12px between controls, 16px panel padding, and 8px inside compact rows.

whiteSpace: Keep the overlay narrow and short so it never covers a host page's buy button or price.
Give the chart 16px padding and leave axes uncluttered; show only 3 to 4 tick labels.
Allow the overlay to collapse to a small pill, leaving almost nothing on screen.

levels.name: Popup base
levels.usage: Popup dashboard background and rows.

levels.name: Card
levels.usage: Tracked item cards in the dashboard.

levels.name: Overlay
levels.usage: In-page overlay panel; strongest separation from unknown host backgrounds.

levels.name: Alert toast
levels.usage: Price-drop notification with Go to product; dismissible and auto-hides.

dropShadow.style: Layered (tight + wide) so it works on both light and dark host pages
dropShadow.notes: Combine the shadow with a 1px border because a shadow alone disappears on dark or busy backgrounds.

visualPriority: Current price and the drop indicator are the largest and highest-contrast elements in the overlay.
The chart line is Indigo; points below target are marked in green.
Notifications sit at the top layer but stay small, dismissible and never block the host page.
